## Why This Is Asked

Deprecations pose production risk in multi-tenant clusters. This question probes practical policy design across CI and runtime using Gatekeeper and Kyverno, plus concrete manifests and validation strategy.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno admission policies
- Kubernetes API deprecations and upgrade paths
- CI validation with kubeconform/kubeval
- Runtime admission controls and auditability

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate (simplified)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sdeprecatedapi
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sDeprecatedAPI
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sdeprecatedapi
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        deprecated := ["apps/v1beta1", "networking.k8s.io/v1beta1"]
        api := input.review.object.apiVersion
        api == deprecated[_]
        msg := sprintf("deprecated apiVersion used: %v", [api])
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (deprecated API)
apiVersion: apps/v1beta1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: old-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/old:1
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (stable API)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: new-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/new:1
```

- How would you extend to cover CRDs and future API regressions?
- How would you surface violations to developers and enforce remediation in PRs?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question demonstrates end-to-end supply chain security expertise: image signing, SBOM provenance tracking, CVE scanning, and runtime verification in a multi-cloud, high-stakes environment. It tests knowledge of Sigstore ecosystem tools and policy enforcement.

- Image signing with Cosign/Sigstore for supply chain integrity
- CycloneDX SBOM generation for component transparency
- CVE scanning integration (e.g., Trivy, Snyk) for vulnerability detection
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy for runtime enforcement
- Canary deployments and rollback strategies in multi-cloud contexts

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`)
```yaml
name: Image Provenance Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-scan-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate CycloneDX SBOM
        uses: cyclonedx/ghcr-create-sbom@v1
        with:
          format: json
          output-file: sbom.json
      
      - name: Run CVE scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: 'ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}'
          format: json
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
      
      - name: Sign image with Cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
        with:
          cosign-version: 'v2'
      - name: Sign image
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
```

### Gatekeeper Policy (`constraint-template.yaml`)
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: requirecosignsignature
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RequireCosignSignature
      targets:
        - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
          rego: |
            package requirecosignsignature
            violation["image is not signed with Cosign"] {
              image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
              notcosign.verify(image)
            }
```

### Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unsigned-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:unsigned-latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Passing Manifest (Signed Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: signed-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Verification Steps
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify SBOM exists
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify against Gatekeeper policy
kubectl get requirecosignsignature
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This task tests practical CI gating for container hygiene: linting with Hadolint and enforcing image tagging discipline across manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Hadolint integration in GitHub Actions
- YAML parsing to inspect image tags
- Regular expressions for pinning (no latest, no -dev) and clear failure messages
- Practical debugging of lint vs. policy failures

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-docker-k8s.yml
name: CI Gate: Dockerfile lint + tag pin
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ '**' ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3
        with:
          dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
      - name: Check pinned image tags
        run: |
          set -e
          if grep -RIn 'image:.*:.*(latest|dev.*)' manifests || true; then
            echo 'Unpinned image tag detected' ; exit 1;
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale this gate to many repos?
- How would you extend checks for other tag policies (sha256 digests)?

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design end-to-end secure supply chain controls in a real-world, multi-region, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It assesses understanding of image signing, policy-as-code enforcement, cross-registry workflows, CI/CD integration, runtime protection mechanisms, and signing key rotation strategies.

## Key Concepts

- **Sigstore Cosign and Rekor**: Provide transparent, audit-logged image signing and verification through a public transparency log, eliminating the need for managing traditional signing keys.
- **Image provenance and attestations**: Deliver cryptographic proof of image origin and build process, ensuring containers originate from trusted sources.
- **Digest pinning**: Prevents tag-based attacks by binding deployments to specific immutable image digests rather than mutable tags.
- **Keyless signing**: Uses OIDC identities (GitHub Actions, Google, Microsoft) for authentication, simplifying key rotation and reducing secret sprawl.
- **Admission controllers**: Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper intercept API requests at admission time, enforcing policy before workloads schedule.

## Security Properties Enforced

| Control | Threat Mitigated |
|---|---|
| Cosign signature verification | Unauthorized image deployment |
| Rekor transparency log | Signing key compromise or repudiation |
| Digest pinning | Tag swap attacks, registry compromise |
| readOnlyRootFilesystem | Container filesystem manipulation |
| runAsNonRoot | Privilege escalation via root |
| noPrivilegeEscalation | Container breakout attempts |

## Multi-Tenant Considerations

For multi-tenant clusters, apply ClusterPolicies with namespace-level exceptions using `generate` rules or leverage OPA's `data.kubernetes.namespace` for tenant-specific policies. Consider combining with admission control annotations for tenant-controlled image allowlists while maintaining platform-wide baseline security.

## Alternatives to Kyverno

OPA Gatekeeper with ConstraintTemplates offers equivalent functionality for teams already invested in the OPA ecosystem, providing Rego-based policy authoring with familiar tooling and broader ecosystem support.

```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snetworkidentity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNetworkIdentityConstraint
  targets:
  - target: Kubernetes
    rego: |
      package k8snetworkidentity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind == "Deployment"

```

```yaml
  name: example-fail
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1

    matchLabels:
      app: example-fail

        app: example-fail
```

```yaml

kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: app-sa
  namespace: dev
  annotations:
    trusted.example.io: "true"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-pass
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-pass
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app-sa
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml

kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-ingress
  namespace: dev
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          env: trusted
```

- Gatekeeper audit run in CI to ensure constraints are evaluated.
- kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f failing.yaml should trigger policy violations.
